sentences.en: Sally said that she walked the dog every day.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I walk the dog every day.') Sally sagte, dass sie jeden Tag den Hund ausführe.

sentences.en: Sally told me that she was walking the dog.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I am walking the dog.') Sally erzählte mir, dass sie gerade den Hund ausführe.

sentences.en: Sally mentioned that she would walk the dog every day.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I will walk the dog every day.') Sally erwähnte, dass sie den Hund jeden Tag ausführen würde.

sentences.en: Sally answered that she had walked the dog the night before.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I walked the dog last night.') Sally antwortete, dass sie den Hund am Abend davor ausgeführt habe.

sentences.en: Sally said that she had walked the dog that day.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I have walked the dog today.') Sally sagte, dass sie den Hund an jenem Tag ausgeführt habe.

sentences.en: Peter said that he was at home.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I'm at home.') Peter sagte, dass er zu Hause sei.

sentences.en: Omar said that he had never been to China.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I've never been to China.') Omar sagte, dass er noch nie in China gewesen sei.

sentences.en: Daniel said that he couldn't speak French.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'I can't speak French.') Daniel sagte, dass er kein Französisch sprechen könne.

sentences.en: The policeman asked the man where he had parked the car.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'Where did you park the car?') Der Polizist fragte den Mann, wo er das Auto geparkt habe.

sentences.en: The policeman asked the man whether it was his car.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'Is this your car?') Der Polizist fragte den Mann, ob es sein Auto sei.

sentences.en: She asked if I was tired.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'Are you tired?') Sie fragte, ob ich müde sei.

sentences.en: Billy asked his brother to take him to the movies.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'Could you take me to the movies?') Billy bat seinen Bruder, ihn ins Kino zu bringen.

sentences.en: Jenny told Michael to hurry up.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'Hurry up!') Jenny sagte Michael, er solle sich beeilen.

sentences.en: Jenny told Michael not to shout that way.
sentences.de: (Direkt: 'Don't shout like that!') Jenny sagte Michael, er solle nicht so schreien.

exercises.title: Martins Ausreden – direkte → indirekte Rede
exercises.instruction: Martin hat Daniella letzte Woche etwas anderes erzählt. Baue Daniellas Antwort in der indirekten Rede.

parts: Letzte Woche: "I have my own business." – Jetzt: "My boss gave me a promotion today!" → Daniella: But I thought you said
your own business.
questions.solutionEn: But I thought you said you had your own business.
questions.solutionDe: Aber ich dachte, du hättest gesagt, du hättest eine eigene Firma.
questions.explain: Backshift: have (Present Simple) → had (Past Simple); Pronomen I → you, weil Daniella Martin direkt anspricht.

parts: Letzte Woche: "I've travelled all over the world." – Jetzt: "I've never been to China." → Daniella: But I thought you told me
all over the world.
questions.solutionEn: But I thought you told me you had travelled all over the world.
questions.solutionDe: Aber ich dachte, du hättest mir erzählt, du seist um die ganze Welt gereist.
questions.explain: Backshift: have travelled (Present Perfect) → had travelled (Past Perfect).

parts: Letzte Woche: "I have a Mercedes." – Jetzt: "I take the train to work every day." → Daniella: But didn't you say
a Mercedes?
questions.solutionEn: But didn't you say you had a Mercedes?
questions.solutionDe: Aber hast du nicht gesagt, du hättest einen Mercedes?
questions.explain: Backshift: have → had (Present → Past). Der Einleitungssatz (didn't you say) steht im Past.

parts: Letzte Woche: "I don't drink alcohol." – Jetzt: "Let's go for a beer tomorrow evening." → Daniella: But you said
alcohol.
questions.solutionEn: But you said you didn't drink alcohol.
questions.solutionDe: Aber du hast gesagt, du trinkst keinen Alkohol.
questions.explain: Backshift: don't drink (Present Simple) → didn't drink (Past Simple). Past Perfect wäre eine Stufe zu viel.

parts: Letzte Woche: "I can speak French fluently." – Jetzt: "The waiters refused to speak English!" → Daniella: But I thought you said
French fluently.
questions.solutionEn: But I thought you said you could speak French fluently.
questions.solutionDe: Aber ich dachte, du hättest gesagt, du könntest fließend Französisch sprechen.
questions.explain: Modalverb-Backshift: can → could.

parts: Letzte Woche: "I live alone." – Jetzt: "Sorry, I have to answer the phone. It's my flatmate." → Daniella: But you told me
alone.
questions.solutionEn: But you told me you lived alone.
questions.solutionDe: Aber du hast mir erzählt, du wohnst allein.
questions.explain: Backshift: live → lived (Present → Past Simple). tell braucht ein Objekt: you told ME.

parts: Letzte Woche: "I'm going to Miami this summer." – Jetzt: "I'm going to stay at home this summer." → Daniella: But didn't you say
to Miami this summer?
questions.solutionEn: But didn't you say you were going to Miami this summer?
questions.solutionDe: Aber hast du nicht gesagt, du würdest diesen Sommer nach Miami fahren?
questions.explain: Backshift: are going (Present Progressive) → were going (Past Progressive). 'this summer' bleibt, weil es noch derselbe Sommer ist.

parts: Letzte Woche: "I won't forget your name." – Jetzt: "It was nice to see you again, Maria." → Daniella: It's Daniella! I thought you said
name.
questions.solutionEn: I thought you said you wouldn't forget my name.
questions.solutionDe: Ich dachte, du hättest gesagt, du würdest meinen Namen nicht vergessen.
questions.explain: Backshift: won't → wouldn't; Pronomen: your name → my name (aus Daniellas Sicht).

exercises.title: Backshift nur wenn nötig
exercises.source: reported-speech student B1-B2 – Practice: Reported statements 1–6
exercises.instruction: Verändere die Zeit NUR, wenn es nötig ist. Achte auf die Zeitangabe im Satz!

parts: Joe said, "I'm going away this week." → Joe said he
that week.
questions.solutionEn: Joe said he was going away that week.
questions.solutionDe: Joe sagte, er verreise in jener Woche.
questions.explain: 'that week' (statt 'this week') zeigt: Die Woche ist vorbei → Backshift: am going → was going.

parts: The athlete said, "I will win the race tomorrow." → The athlete said he
tomorrow.
questions.solutionEn: The athlete said he will win the race tomorrow.
questions.solutionDe: Der Athlet sagte, er wird das Rennen morgen gewinnen.
questions.explain: 'tomorrow' bleibt im Satz → das Rennen ist immer noch morgen, die Situation ist unverändert → KEIN Backshift. 'would win' wäre nur richtig, wenn aus tomorrow 'the next day' würde.

parts: The news reporter said, "People have been protesting in the streets today." → The news reporter said people
in the streets that day.
questions.solutionEn: The news reporter said people had been protesting in the streets that day.
questions.solutionDe: Der Reporter sagte, die Menschen hätten an jenem Tag auf den Straßen protestiert.
questions.explain: 'that day' → Situation vorbei → Backshift: Present Perfect Progressive → Past Perfect Progressive.

parts: The director said, "The company will continue to grow next year." → The director said the company
next year.
questions.solutionEn: The director said the company will continue to grow next year.
questions.solutionDe: Der Direktor sagte, die Firma wird nächstes Jahr weiter wachsen.
questions.explain: 'next year' bleibt → die Aussage gilt noch → KEIN Backshift nötig.

parts: Last year, the doctor said, "You need to rest more." → Last year, the doctor told me I
questions.solutionEn: Last year, the doctor told me I needed to rest more.
questions.solutionDe: Letztes Jahr sagte mir der Arzt, ich müsse mich mehr ausruhen.
questions.explain: 'Last year' → liegt lange zurück → Backshift: need → needed. Pronomen: you → I.

parts: The president said, "I won't lose the election." → The president said he
, but he did.
questions.solutionEn: The president said he wouldn't lose the election, but he did.
questions.solutionDe: Der Präsident sagte, er würde die Wahl nicht verlieren – aber er hat sie verloren.
questions.explain: 'but he did' → die Situation hat sich geändert (er hat doch verloren) → Backshift: won't → wouldn't.

exercises.title: Zeitverschiebung – der Backshift-Trainer
exercises.instruction: Der Einleitungssatz steht im Past – wähle die richtige Zeitform für die indirekte Rede.

parts: Present Simple: She said, "I drink a coke." → She said that she
a coke.
questions.solutionEn: She said that she drank a coke.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, dass sie eine Cola trinke.
questions.explain: Present Simple → Past Simple (drink → drank).

parts: Present Progressive: Sally said, "I am walking the dog." → Sally said that she
the dog.
questions.solutionEn: Sally said that she was walking the dog.
questions.solutionDe: Sally sagte, dass sie gerade den Hund ausführe.
questions.explain: Present Progressive → Past Progressive (am walking → was walking).

parts: Past Simple: She said, "I drank a coke." → She said that she
a coke.
questions.solutionEn: She said that she had drunk a coke.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, dass sie eine Cola getrunken habe.
questions.explain: Past Simple → Past Perfect (drank → had drunk).

parts: Present Perfect: She said, "I have drunk a coke." → She said that she
a coke.
questions.solutionEn: She said that she had drunk a coke.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, dass sie eine Cola getrunken habe.
questions.explain: Present Perfect → Past Perfect (have drunk → had drunk).

parts: will-Future: She said, "I will drink a coke." → She said that she
a coke.
questions.solutionEn: She said that she would drink a coke.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, dass sie eine Cola trinken würde.
questions.explain: will → would; nach would steht immer der Infinitiv (drink, nicht drank).

parts: going-to-Future: She said, "I am going to drink a coke." → She said that she
a coke.
questions.solutionEn: She said that she was going to drink a coke.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, dass sie eine Cola trinken werde.
questions.explain: going-to-Future: am/is going to → was/were going to.

parts: Modalverb can: Tom said, "I can help you." → Tom said that he
me.
questions.solutionEn: Tom said that he could help me.
questions.solutionDe: Tom sagte, dass er mir helfen könne.
questions.explain: Modalverb: can → could; Pronomen: I → he, you → me.

parts: Modalverb may: She said, "I may be late." → She said that she
late.
questions.solutionEn: She said that she might be late.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, dass sie vielleicht zu spät kommen könnte.
questions.explain: Modalverb: may → might.

parts: Fakten: He said, "The Rhine flows through Vorarlberg." → He said that the Rhine
through Vorarlberg.
questions.solutionEn: He said that the Rhine flows through Vorarlberg.
questions.solutionDe: Er sagte, dass der Rhein durch Vorarlberg fließt.
questions.explain: Allgemeine Fakten und Wahrheiten: KEINE Zeitverschiebung nötig.

parts: Einleitungssatz im Present: Frank says, "Mary buys new shoes." → Frank says that Mary
new shoes.
questions.solutionEn: Frank says that Mary buys new shoes.
questions.solutionDe: Frank sagt, dass Mary neue Schuhe kauft.
questions.explain: Einleitungsverb im Present/Present Perfect/Future (says) → KEIN Backshift.

exercises.title: Zeit- und Ortsangaben
exercises.instruction: Wähle die richtige Zeit- bzw. Ortsangabe für die indirekte Rede.

parts: "I am busy now," she said. → She said she was busy
questions.solutionEn: She said she was busy then.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, sie sei da gerade beschäftigt.
questions.explain: now → then.

parts: "I saw him yesterday," Tom said. → Tom said he had seen him
questions.solutionEn: Tom said he had seen him the day before.
questions.solutionDe: Tom sagte, er habe ihn am Tag davor gesehen.
questions.explain: yesterday → the day before / the previous day; außerdem Backshift saw → had seen.

parts: "We will meet tomorrow," they said. → They said they would meet
questions.solutionEn: They said they would meet the next day.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagten, sie würden sich am nächsten Tag treffen.
questions.explain: tomorrow → the next day / the following day.

parts: "I like it here," Ann said. → Ann said she liked it
questions.solutionEn: Ann said she liked it there.
questions.solutionDe: Ann sagte, es gefalle ihr dort.
questions.explain: here → there.

parts: "I am leaving today," he said. → He said he was leaving
questions.solutionEn: He said he was leaving that day.
questions.solutionDe: Er sagte, er reise an jenem Tag ab.
questions.explain: today → that day.

parts: "I bought this car last week," he said. → He said he had bought
car
questions.solutionEn: He said he had bought that car the week before.
questions.solutionDe: Er sagte, er habe jenes Auto in der Woche davor gekauft.
questions.explain: this → that; last week → the week before / the previous week.

parts: "We are moving next week," she said. → She said they were moving
questions.solutionEn: She said they were moving the following week.
questions.solutionDe: Sie sagte, sie würden in der folgenden Woche umziehen.
questions.explain: next week → the following week; Pronomen: we → they.

parts: "I started my job a year ago," he said. → He said he had started his job
questions.solutionEn: He said he had started his job the previous year.
questions.solutionDe: Er sagte, er habe seinen Job im Jahr davor begonnen.
questions.explain: a year ago → the previous year / the year before; außerdem Backshift started → had started.

parts: He said, "Where do you buy your car?" → He wanted to know where I
my car.
questions.solutionEn: He wanted to know where I bought my car.
questions.solutionDe: Er wollte wissen, wo ich mein Auto kaufe.
questions.explain: Fragewort (where) bleibt; Aussagesatz-Wortstellung ohne do; Backshift: buy → bought; Pronomen: you → I.

parts: She said, "Are you tired?" → She asked
I
tired.
questions.solutionEn: She asked if I was tired.
questions.solutionDe: Sie fragte, ob ich müde sei.
questions.explain: Frage OHNE Fragewort → if/whether (= ob); Backshift: are → was.

parts: "Where did you park the car?" → The policeman asked the man where
the car.
questions.solutionEn: The policeman asked the man where he had parked the car.
questions.solutionDe: Der Polizist fragte den Mann, wo er das Auto geparkt habe.
questions.explain: Indirekte Frage = Aussagesatz-Wortstellung (Subjekt VOR Verb), kein did; Past Simple → Past Perfect.

parts: Höfliche Bitte: She said, "Help me, please." → She
me
her.
questions.solutionEn: She asked me to help her.
questions.solutionDe: Sie bat mich, ihr zu helfen.
questions.explain: Höfliche Bitte (please) → ask + Objekt + to-Infinitiv; Pronomen: me → her.

parts: Aufforderung: She said, "Help me." → She
me to help her.
questions.solutionEn: She told me to help her.
questions.solutionDe: Sie forderte mich auf, ihr zu helfen.
questions.explain: Normale Aufforderung → tell + Objekt + to-Infinitiv.

parts: Verneinte Aufforderung: Jenny said, "Don't shout like that!" → Jenny told Michael
that way.
questions.solutionEn: Jenny told Michael not to shout that way.
questions.solutionDe: Jenny sagte Michael, er solle nicht so schreien.
questions.explain: Verneinte Aufforderung → told + Objekt + NOT + to-Infinitiv. 'not' steht VOR 'to'.

parts: Bitte: Billy said, "Could you take me to the movies?" → Billy asked his brother
him to the movies.
questions.solutionEn: Billy asked his brother to take him to the movies.
questions.solutionDe: Billy bat seinen Bruder, ihn ins Kino zu bringen.
questions.explain: Bitte (Could you ...?) → ask + Objekt + to-Infinitiv; Pronomen: me → him.

parts: Vorschlag: Alex said, "Let's go to the cinema." → Alex suggested
to the cinema.
questions.solutionEn: Alex suggested going to the cinema.
questions.solutionDe: Alex schlug vor, ins Kino zu gehen.
questions.explain: suggest + Verb-ing (oder: suggested that we go). 'suggested to go' ist FALSCH.
